He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball|Saint Mary's Gaels]]. ==Early life== Ford learned the game of chess at the age of four with his father, Cuzear, serving as his teacher. He began beating adults before winning two California state titles and was ranked seventh in the nation in his age bracket. However, he quit playing competitively at the age of eight to focus on basketball.{{cite news |last=Bennett |first=Brian |title=Jordan Ford and Saint Mary's may be in line for their best season yet. Here's why |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1274620/2019/10/08/jordan-ford-and-saint-marys-may-be-in-line-for-their-best-season-yet-heres-why/ |access-date=December 9, 2019 |work=[[The Athletic]] |date=October 8, 2019}} Ford attended [[Folsom High School]], playing under coach Mike Wall. He scored 34 points in a playoff game against [[Sacramento High School]] in March 2016. He was named ''[[The Sacramento Bee]]''{{'s}} player of the year twice.{{cite news |last=Stites |first=Brian |title=Former Chess Champion Now The King Of Saint Mary's Backcourt |url=https://sanfrancisco.cbslocal.com/2017/12/20/former-chess-champion-now-the-king-of-saint-marys-backcourt/ |accessdate=December 9, 2019 |work=CBS |date=December 20, 2017}} He committed to play for [[Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball|Saint Mary's]] because he liked the structured offense, spurning offers from [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]], [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]], [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] and [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]].{{cite news |last=Kroichick |first=Rom |title=St. Mary's Jordan Ford taking spin in spotlight |url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/collegesports/article/St-Mary-s-Jordan-Ford-taking-spin-in-spotlight-12762859.php |accessdate=December 9, 2019 |work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] |date=March 18, 2019}} ==College career== As a freshman, Ford considered redshirting, but ultimately came off the bench as a backup to Joe Rahon, who encouraged him to focus on his defense. In the summer of 2017, Ford was diagnosed with [[epiglottitis]] and ended up in the hospital, losing the 12 pounds he gained lifting weights. He scored 27 against [[2017–18 BYU Cougars men's basketball team|BYU]] in the [[2018 West Coast Conference men's basketball tournament|2018 West Coast Conference (WCC) tournament]]. Ford had 19 points against [[2017–18 Southeastern Louisiana Lions basketball team|Southeastern Louisiana]] in the first round of the [[2018 NIT]] and made a SportsCenter top-10 play when he took a pass from [[Emmett Naar]] and did a double-spin move to complete a layup off the glass. As a sophomore, Ford averaged 11.1 points, 2.7 rebounds, and 1.6 assists per game, shooting 50.8 percent from the field and 44.3 percent from behind the arc.{{cite news |last=Johnson |first=Raphielle |title=WCC Conference Preview: Can anyone threaten Gonzaga? |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2018/11/02/wcc-conference-preview-can-anyone-threaten-gonzaga/ |accessdate=December 9, 2019 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=November 2, 2018}} Ford scored a career-high 35 points on 11-of-17 shooting in a 92–63 win over [[2018–19 Utah Valley Wolverines men's basketball team|Utah Valley]] on November 13, 2018.{{cite news |title=Ford scores 35 points, Saint Mary's beats Utah Valley 92–63 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401083726 |accessdate=December 9, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}} As a junior, Ford was second in the WCC in scoring with 21.1 points per game to go with 2.5 assists, 2.8 rebounds, and 1.3 steals per game. He helped lead the Gaels to an upset over [[2018–19 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga]] in the [[2019 West Coast Conference men's basketball tournament|2019 WCC championship]] and [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] appearance, where they fell to [[2018–19 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]].{{cite news |last=Land |first=Sam |title=Three Saint Mary's players who Badger fans need to know |url=https://badgerswire.usatoday.com/2019/11/04/three-saint-marys-players-who-badger-fans-need-to-know/ |accessdate=December 9, 2019 |work=Badgers Wire |date=November 4, 2019}} He was named to the First Team All-WCC.{{cite news|title=WCC Announces 2018–19 Men's Basketball All-Conference Team|url=https://wccsports.com/news/2019/3/5/wcc-announces-2018-19-mens-basketball-all-conference-team.aspx|accessdate=March 5, 2019|work=[[West Coast Conference]]|date=March 5, 2019}} Coming into his senior season, Ford was named to the [[Naismith Award|Naismith]] and [[Wooden Award]] watchlists. In his senior season opener, he scored 26 points and hit 4-of-8 three-pointers as Saint Mary's defeated [[2019–20 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]] 65–63 in overtime.{{cite news |title=Ford, No. 18 St. Mary's ready for weary Winthrop |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/ford-no-18-st-marys-ready-for-weary-winthrop/ |accessdate=December 9, 2019 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=November 11, 2019}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Ford was named to the First Team All-WCC.{{cite press release|url=https://wccsports.com/news/2020/3/3/wcc-announces-2019-20-mens-basketball-all-conference-team-mbb.aspx |title=WCC Announces 2019–20 Men's Basketball All-Conference Team |publisher=West Coast Conference |date=March 3, 2020 |accessdate=March 3, 2020}} On March 7, 2020, Ford scored a career-high 42 points in a 89–82 double-overtime win over [[2019–20 Pepperdine Waves men's basketball team|Pepperdine]] in the [[2020 West Coast Conference men's basketball tournament|2020 WCC tournament]] quarterfinal.{{cite news |title=Ford has 42, Ross 43 as Saint Mary's trips Pepp in 2 OT |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401211161 |accessdate=March 9, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=March 8, 2020}} He scored 18 points in the WCC tournament semifinal versus [[2019–20 BYU Cougars men's basketball team|BYU]] and hit a jump shot with 1.4 seconds remaining to give the Gaels a 51–50 win.{{cite news |title=Saint Mary's slips past No. 14 BYU 51–50 in WCC semifinal |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401211163 |accessdate=March 10, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=March 10, 2020}} Ford averaged 21.9 points per game on a team that finished 26–8.{{cite news |last=Sung |first=Elaine |title=The 2020 NCAA tournament that could have been: Midwest region |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/2020/03/16/2020-ncaa-tournament-march-madness-midwest-region/5052904002/ |accessdate=March 25, 2020 |work=[[Detroit Free Press]] |date=March 16, 2020}} 18, 2020}} He was waived by the Clippers on December 14.
